questions.question: What will help someone who has drunk alcohol feel normal again?
questions.explanation: Only time will allow a person's body to get over the effects of alcohol.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is correct?

options.text: It is illegal to drive around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red signals and gates.

questions.explanation: You must stop when a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices like gates or flashing lights tell you to. Some railroad crossings do not have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad gates.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions and dangers. This sign warns drivers that buggies may be ahead.

questions.question: How can you stay out of a truck or bus driver's blind spot?

options.text: Don't drive next to them and don't drive too close behind them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't drive next to them and don't drive too close behind them.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles like trucks and buses have large blind spots on the sides and rear. Don't drive next to them and don't tailgate them.

questions.question: What must a driver do to safely pass another vehicle?

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and briefly look at the lane you want to enter. Make sure no other car is in your blind spot and that there is enough room to move safely.

questions.question: Anything that forces you to ____ could cause a crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel

questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that makes you take your attention away from driving, take your eyes off the road, or take your hands off the wheel.

questions.question: As you approach an intersection, the light turns yellow. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to go through before it turns red.
Be ready to stop in the middle of the intersection.
Be ready to stop before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming soon. Be ready to stop safely before you reach the intersection.

questions.question: When stopped by police for a traffic violation or inspection, you must show:
questions.explanation: You must carry and show your license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance when driving. Police can ask for all three documents during a traffic stop or inspection.

questions.question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, you must:

options.text: Pull over to the side and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, pull over to the curb or side of the road and stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means left turns are not allowed.

questions.question: The best way to avoid hydroplaning is to:

options.text: Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.
Watch out for standing water or puddles.

questions.explanation: Wet roads make your car take longer to stop and can cause skidding on sharp turns. Do not use cruise control on wet or icy roads. Reduce your speed and drive carefully.

questions.question: When a school bus stops with its stop arm extended, you should:

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
Honk your horn before passing the bus on its left.
Keep driving when you think most children have exited the bus.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
questions.explanation: When a school bus displays its stop signal, you must come to a complete stop. Do not proceed until the stop arm is withdrawn.

questions.question: When it starts to sleet or snow, you should:

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.
Leave more space between your vehicle and the vehicles ahead.

questions.explanation: In snow, keep your windshield and mirrors clear. Increase your following distance in wet and cold weather because slippery roads require more distance to stop.

questions.question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is likely to be:

options.text: A person conducting a traffic study.

questions.explanation: You must always yield the right-of-way to a blind person using a white cane or guide dog.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead turns sharply right, then left.
The road ahead turns sharply left, then right.
The road ahead curves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road will turn sharply to the right and then to the left.

questions.question: The 'No zone' is:

options.text: The blind spots around a truck or bus.
A roadway with restrictions on vehicle stereo volume.
The television show that replaced The Twilight Zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spots around a truck or bus.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on each side, in the rear, and in the front. Your car cannot be seen in these areas. These blind spots are called the 'No zone.'

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal, even when no other traffic is visible.
Signal only if there is visible traffic.
Signal only when driving at night.
Signal only when driving in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even when no other traffic is visible.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes, turning, or pulling away from a curb. Do not develop bad habits by failing to follow this law.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing with no train visible or audible, you must stop if:
questions.explanation: You must stop before crossing railroad tracks if flashing red lights are on, a gate is lowered, a stop sign is posted, a flagger signals you to stop, or a train is visible or close enough to be unsafe. If you are unsure, stop. Never race a train.

questions.question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes:

options.text: Look into the left side mirror.
Look into the right side mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
questions.explanation: To check your blind spot, look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.question: When you see a steady red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through if there is no crossing traffic.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.

questions.explanation: A steady red light means you must come to a complete stop. Driving through a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on red if no sign prohibits it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you to stay to the right of the divider.

questions.question: When driving on wet pavement, remember:

options.text: Roads are slippery right after rain starts.
You need extra space to stop.

questions.explanation: Wet roads are slippery because of a thin layer of oil, dirt, and water. Slow down when roads are wet, have standing water, or have slush to keep your wheels from sliding.

questions.question: Alcohol causes:
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol hurts your vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination.

questions.question: You hear a siren behind you. You should:

options.text: Pull over to the right and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights behind you, safely move to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in heavy traffic, drive slowly until you can move out of the way.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing red or blue lights?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before it catches you.
Keep driving but try to stay out of the way.
Pull over to the side and come to a complete stop.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side and come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: You must yield to all emergency vehicles with sirens or flashing lights. Pull over to the right edge of the road when possible. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first before pulling over.

questions.question: Braking distance is affected by:

options.text: The condition of your brakes and tires.

questions.explanation: Braking distance depends on your speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This regulation sign tells drivers in the left lane that they must turn left.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the direction to drive when entering a one-way street.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you a playground is near. Watch for children on or near the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This orange construction sign warns you about work zones. It tells you that penalties are doubled for unsafe driving in work zones.
